title: Target locality reduces the single-complex criterion to affine bases
statement: Fix a family of derived categories of sheaves of modules on schemes [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose the single-complex derived base-change criterion holds for every cartesian square with both bases affine, f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, K,K' quasi-coherent in the derived sense, and φ:L(g')*K→K' satisfying the stalk condition [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Then that criterion holds for arbitrary bases: for every such cartesian square with no affineness assumptions, the canonical composite Lg*Rf*K→Rf'*L(g')*K→Rf'*K' [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] is invertible. The affine-base criterion is a premise, not asserted unconditionally by this lemma.

source.place: Tag 0DJ9 (lemma-single-complex-base-change), first paragraph, reduction to affine bases

proof.text: For x in S' choose an affine open V of S containing g(x), then an affine open V' of S' containing x and contained in g inverse-image V, using Mathlib exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset. Construct j as the restriction of g' from f' inverse-image V' to f inverse-image V. The original commutativity proves the required containment. Scheme.Hom.isPullback_resLE constructs the restricted cartesian square; the restricted f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the Mathlib restriction instances.

Define K0 and K0' by exact open restriction. Apply schemeDerivedQCoh_openRestriction_iff to each; in each cohomological degree use SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_over to restrict the original quasi-coherent cohomology sheaf. Construct phi0 by singleComplexRestrictedCoefficient. No object or coefficient map is selected from a mere existence theorem.

Apply singleComplexBaseChange_openRestrictionComparison to the constructed square. It gives the stalk condition for the explicitly constructed phi0 and source and target isomorphisms identifying its base-change composite with the restricted original composite. Apply h_affine to the affine bases V,V', the restricted f, the two explicitly restricted quasi-coherent objects, and phi0. Rewrite the comparison equality; composition with the source and target isomorphisms shows the restricted original composite is an isomorphism.
Every point x has the resulting neighbourhood V'. Apply schemeDerived_isIso_of_openRestriction to the original composite. On an empty S' the pointwise premise is vacuous, as required.
